paper.title: Coordinating the Unknown Lipschitz Constant in Multiplayer Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Problem A: unobserved actions, common rewards
unmapped: Lipschitz constant L (w.r.t. sup norm) unknown to players
f twice differentiable with Hessian bounded by unknown N_hess
joint action space [0,1]^{Nd}, each player chooses its own d-dim coordinate block
no communication after learning starts (shared randomness allowed beforehand)
players receive a common reward but do not observe others' actions
settings.definition_quote: Problem A: unobserved actions, common rewards. Every player receives the same reward $Y_{t}$ but does not observe the actions of the others.

settings.name_in_paper: Problem B: observed actions, independent rewards
unmapped: Lipschitz constant L (w.r.t. sup norm) unknown to players
f twice differentiable with Hessian bounded by unknown N_hess
players observe all actions but receive i.i.d. independent private rewards
settings.definition_quote: Problem B: observed actions, independent rewards. Every player observes the actions of all others, but rewards are i.i.d. across players and player $i$ sees only its own reward $Y_t^i$.

settings.name_in_paper: Problem C: unobserved actions, independent rewards
unmapped: Lipschitz constant L (w.r.t. sup norm) unknown to players
f twice differentiable with Hessian bounded by unknown N_hess
no communication after learning starts (shared dither agreed beforehand)
actions unobserved and rewards i.i.d. private across players
settings.definition_quote: Problem C: unobserved actions, independent rewards. The two difficulties combine: rewards are i.i.d. across players and actions are unobserved.

algorithms.name: mECAB with action signalling and subroutine of chang2023optimal (Problem B)
mECAB with dithered quantization of L estimate (Problem C)

source.label: regret_A
source.quote: Let $m \geq 8N/L$ and use \texttt{m-UCB} of~\cite{chang2021multiplayer} with $\widehat{L}$ from~\eqref{discretization_A}. Then \texttt{mECAB} satisfies $\sup_{\mathcal{F}_{L,N}}R_{T} \leq T^{(Md+1)/(Md+2)} \cdot (9L^{Md/(Md+2)} + 5(2m\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{E}\ln(2T^{Md+1})})^{Md/(Md+2)}) + Em^{Md}+32\sqrt{T\widetilde{m}^{Md}\log T} + 1.$

results.notes: Sup over class F_{L,N}. Bound contains the random/data-dependent m_tilde; paper notes on high-prob event this term is O(T^{(Md+1)/(Md+2)}(L+1)^{Md/(Md+2)} sqrt(log T)). Proof chooses m = floor(T^alpha) and E accordingly.

source.label: regret_B
source.quote: Let $m \geq 8N/L$ and use the multiplayer subroutine of~\cite{chang2023optimal} for Problem~B. Then \texttt{mECAB} satisfies $\sup_{\mathcal{F}_{L,N}} R_{T} \leq T^{(Md+1)/(Md+2)} \times (9L^{Md/(Md+2)} + 5(2m\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{ME}\ln(2T^{Md+1})})^{Md/(Md+2)}) + Em^{Md}+ 32\sqrt{T\widetilde{m}^{Md}\log T} + 1.$

results.notes: Same as Theorem 4 with E replaced by ME inside the sqrt (pooling). Bound contains data-dependent m_tilde.

source.label: regret_C
source.quote: Let $m \geq 8N/L$, let $A = 4M(2m)^{Md}$, and use the multiplayer subroutine of~\cite{chang2021multiplayer} with $\widehat L$ from~\eqref{discretization_C}. Then $\sup R_{T} \leq T^{(Md+1)/(Md+2)} \times (9L^{Md/(Md+2)} + 5(2m\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{E}\ln(2T^{Md+1})})^{Md/(Md+2)}) + Em^{Md}+ C\log T\sqrt{T\widetilde{m}^{Md}} + 17\,Tm\sqrt{\ln(A)/E}.$ In particular, if $E \geq m^{2}T^{2/(Md+2)}\ln A$ the last term is at most $17\,T^{(Md+1)/(Md+2)}$.

results.notes: Last term pays for disagreement among players' quantized L estimates. Bound contains data-dependent m_tilde and unspecified constant C.
